subject: Enterprise SLA language alignment (Escalation Playbook v2) — approvals + exception handling
related_links: Confluence: Escalation Playbook v2 > Support and Eng SLAs by tier (draft)
body:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Enterprise SLA language alignment (Escalation Playbook v2) — approvals + exception handling

Team — we need to lock external-facing SLA language today so CS/Sales are consistent (and so we don’t promise more than what SRE can operationally support).

I’m attaching a v3 draft of the enterprise SLA language (intended to be “safe to share” in MSAs/order forms and enterprise onboarding docs) + a screenshot of the draft SLA table from the playbook.

Open items I need alignment on (esp. for Dedicated + Private):
1) 24/7 coverage wording: are we saying “24/7 for Sev0/Sev1 only” or “24/7 first response for all severities for enterprise?”
2) Time-to-mitigation: do we keep this as a target (“target mitigation within X”) vs a commitment? (I lean target.)
3) Update cadence: can we commit to update frequency by severity without causing paging noise?
4) Exceptions / one-off commitments: what’s our approval path (CS leadership + SRE oncall manager + CRO?) and how do we document it (addendum vs email)?

If you can reply with edits/concerns by 11:30am, I’ll loop Jordan for final sign-off before EOD.

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
VP Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Enterprise_SLA_Language_v3.docx
Attachment: Escalation_Playbook_v2_SLA_Table_Screenshot.png


From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Enterprise SLA language alignment (Escalation Playbook v2) — approvals + exception handling

Agree with your lean on “targets” vs “commitments” for mitigation.

CS perspective / where we’ve gotten burned:
- Some CSMs have been saying “we monitor 24/7” and customers hear “any issue gets immediate engineering.” We should explicitly narrow the 24/7 coverage to Sev0/Sev1 only.
- For Sev2+, we should explicitly say “business hours response unless otherwise stated in order form.” (We can still be responsive in practice without it becoming a contractual expectation.)

Suggested customer-facing phrasing (simple and unambiguous):
- “24/7 incident response for Sev0/Sev1 impacting production workloads.”
- “Sev2/Sev3 handled during regional business hours; we will use reasonable efforts to respond sooner as available.”

Exception handling: I’d like a clear rule that any SLA exception that changes coverage (e.g., “24/7 for Sev2”) needs CRO signoff because it impacts commercial expectations and renewals.

One more note: Dedicated customers often ask for “latency SLA” — we should keep that out of the support SLA language and point them to the specific SLA exhibit if they purchased it.

Rachel


From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: Enterprise SLA language alignment (Escalation Playbook v2) — approvals + exception handling

+1 to narrowing 24/7 to Sev0/Sev1.

From SRE/oncall side:
- Update cadence commitments are fine IF they’re scoped to declared incidents / Sev0-1 escalations. We should avoid language that implies an engineer is paging for every Sev2 support thread.
- “Time-to-mitigation” cannot be a hard commitment across all failure modes (capacity constraints, cloud provider issues, customer networking issues in Private). Recommend wording:
  - “target time to mitigation” and “we will provide workarounds when full remediation is not immediately available.”

Also recommend we explicitly separate:
- Support first response SLA (CS/support acknowledges, starts triage)
- Engineering engagement SLA (when we pull in SRE/runtime/private deployments)

That separation matters for paging hygiene and for setting expectations in Private (where many issues are customer-env dependent).

If helpful, here’s wording I’ve used in past that customers accept:
- “24/7 coverage applies to Severity 0/1 service incidents attributable to Redwood.”
- “Customer configuration issues and third-party outages may be handled on a best-effort basis with guidance and next steps.”

Sean
Director of SRE


From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:11 AM PST
Subject: SLA language (enterprise) — request for sign-off + exception policy

Jordan — looping you in for CRO sign-off.

We’re finalizing external-facing support SLA language as part of Escalation Playbook v2 (Support/CS + SRE alignment). Goal is consistency + avoid accidental over-commitments in customer threads.

Key decisions we’re proposing:
1) 24/7 coverage scope:
   - Explicitly 24/7 for Sev0/Sev1 production-impacting incidents attributable to Redwood.
   - Sev2/Sev3 handled during regional business hours unless a paid SLA exhibit/order form says otherwise.

2) Mitigation language:
   - “Target time-to-mitigation” (not a guarantee). We commit to investigation + regular updates; remediation/mitigation depends on root cause.

3) Update cadence:
   - We can commit to update frequency for Sev0/Sev1 incidents; avoid implying engineering paging for Sev2 support threads.

4) Exception handling:
   - Any SLA exception changing coverage (e.g., “24/7 for Sev2” or bespoke mitigation timelines) requires approval from CS leadership + SRE leadership + CRO, and should be documented in an order-form addendum (preferred) or a formal written amendment.

Ask:
- Can you confirm you’re good with the above scoping and exception approval path?
- Any guidance on how you want AEs/CSMs to message “targets” vs “commitments” in renewal/expansion conversations?

Draft doc: [Drive: Enterprise SLA Language (working doc)]
Related ticket: Linear PM-612

Thanks,
Jasmine


From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 12:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: SLA language (enterprise) — request for sign-off + exception policy

Approved on the scoping.

Strong preference:
- 24/7 only for Sev0/Sev1 and only when it’s attributable to Redwood.
- Anything broader must be paid for and written into an exhibit. If we ever do an exception, it needs to be time-bound and tied to commercial terms (renewal, expansion, etc.).

On the “targets” language: AEs/CSMs should be coached to avoid numerical promises in email unless it’s contractual. We can say:
- “We acknowledge quickly and we’ll keep you updated on a defined cadence”
- “We will prioritize mitigation; timeline depends on root cause and may involve a workaround first.”

Exception approvals:
- Agree: CS leader + SRE leader + CRO.
- Also add: any exception involving credits/fees needs Finance copied (even if just for awareness). Doesn’t need to be on every incident, just if we’re committing to credits or penalties.

Can we add a one-pager for field teams: “what we can say / what we can’t say” + examples? That will reduce drift.

Jordan
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference


From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 3:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: SLA language (enterprise) — request for sign-off + exception policy

Thanks all — I updated the draft with the agreed scoping and exception policy.

Edits incorporated:
- “24/7 incident response” explicitly limited to Sev0/Sev1, production-impacting, attributable to Redwood.
- “Target time-to-mitigation” language (no guarantee); added explicit “workaround first” option.
- Clarified the separation between Support first response vs Engineering engagement.
- Exception path: CS leader + SRE leader + CRO; Finance looped when credits/fees are part of the exception.

Next steps:
1) Rachel — can you draft the requested field one-pager (“what we can/can’t say” + examples) and I’ll review tomorrow AM? We’ll distribute to AEs/CSMs alongside the playbook rollout.
2) Dev — please make sure the Confluence SLA tables match the external language (no “24/7 for all”).
3) Sean — please sanity-check the Sev0/Sev1 update cadence phrasing one last time for paging hygiene.

Final sign-off request: if anyone sees issues with the revised doc by 10am tomorrow, reply-all; otherwise I’ll mark this as approved and we’ll proceed with PM-612.

Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
VP Customer Success | Redwood Inference
